commits.message:
feat(docs): /playground is the card at full width (rich-example-card-obsb.cau)

The playground is the example card: line numbers on, setup unfolded, the
edited line always shown, the program in the hash. Try it carries the card's
program, setup groups included (card.<deflated JSON>); a hash in the old
format opens as a program with no setup.

The card decides how to show a playground program from what it does: a
static run is drawn; one that redraws, listens on stdin, leaves a timer
running past its body, or is still running at the limit moves to the live
terminal. RichPlayground.ts is deleted.

feat(docs): live blocks are editable cards running in the live terminal (rich-example-card-obsb.2pn) (#355)

* feat(docs): live blocks are editable cards running in the live terminal (rich-example-card-obsb.2pn)

A live block is now RichExample's third card kind: its outlet is a live
terminal (LiveScreen, the old RichLive taking a program instead of a
module) running the card's program, made in the browser as an edit's is.
An edit that parses restarts the terminal on it; one that does not is said
in red over the terminal it leaves running.

The build no longer bundles a program per live block; it checks each live
card's programs import only what the live library holds.

* fix(docs): the build compiles a live card's program as the browser does (rich-example-card-obsb.2pn)

- playgroundProgram asks the eval's parser for its compiled code, so
  import.meta is refused for an edit and at build alike.
- The build reads what a live program requires off Sucrase's output: an
  import only of types is no longer refused, an elided one never was.
- LiveScreen makes a terminal and clears a failure only for the newest ask.
- A live card's page program is made once; reset hands that program back,
  and the page's own code shows at once rather than after the debounce.
